question: What is the main reason nurses wear medical gloves when caring for patients?

options.A: To act as a physical barrier against microorganisms
options.B: To prevent skin irritation from harsh hospital soaps
options.C: To keep the hands of the nurse warm and dry
options.D: To replace the need for routine hand hygiene

explanation: You've got this! Gloves act like a shield, stopping germs from passing back and forth between you and your patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must you wash your hands right after taking off a pair of gloves?

options.A: Hospital policy mandates double washing after every procedure
options.B: Gloves make the skin completely waterproof and prone to sweat
options.C: Soap removes the sticky powder residue left behind by latex
options.D: Microbes multiply quickly on the warm skin trapped inside gloves

explanation: Great thinking! The warm, sweaty environment inside used gloves is a cozy home for bacteria, so always clean your hands after taking them off. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which of these everyday clinical tasks means you definitely need to put on clean medical gloves?

options.A: Emptying a urinary drainage bag from a catheter
options.B: Handing out oral tablets in paper medication cups
options.C: Feeding a patient with a stable swallowing reflex
options.D: Taking a routine blood pressure reading on intact skin

explanation: Spot on! Whenever you might touch body fluids like urine, gloves are a must to keep things clean and safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: When is it totally fine for a nurse to skip wearing gloves?

options.A: While checking the blood pressure of a patient with intact skin
options.B: While providing perineal hygiene for an incontinent adult
options.C: During the insertion of an indwelling urinary catheter
options.D: When cleaning up a major blood spill on the floor

explanation: Spot on! If skin is unbroken and there are no body fluids around, basic tasks like taking a BP don't require gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is a major difference between regular examination gloves and surgical gloves?

options.A: Examination gloves are always manufactured using natural rubber latex
options.B: Surgical gloves come in precise fractional sizes for a snug fit
options.C: Examination gloves are completely sterile straight out of the box
options.D: Surgical gloves can be washed and autoclaved for reuse later

explanation: You got it! Surgical gloves are measured precisely so surgeons and scrub nurses have maximum feel and control during sterile procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: You are getting ready to insert a sterile urinary catheter. Which gloves should you grab?

options.A: Sterile surgical gloves that fit the hands precisely
options.B: Clean utility gloves made from thick nitrile material
options.C: Non-sterile examination gloves from a wall dispenser
options.D: Heavy-duty utility gloves used for washing instruments

explanation: Brilliant! Because catheter insertion goes deep into the urinary tract, you need truly sterile gloves to prevent introducing any germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which glove material is tough against chemicals and makes a great allergy-safe substitute for latex?
explanation: Exactly! Nitrile is strong, resists punctures well, and is a lifesaver for people with latex allergies. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why are vinyl gloves usually kept for short, low-risk tasks?

options.A: It triggers severe allergic reactions more often than latex
options.B: It is too expensive for routine use in under-resourced wards
options.C: It breaks down easily and has lower elasticity and durability
options.D: It completely eliminates tactile sensitivity for the wearer

explanation: Spot on! Vinyl doesn't stretch well and tears easily, so we save it only for quick, low-risk duties. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you must do before putting on a pair of examination gloves?

options.A: Apply sterile talcum powder to the hands
options.C: Wipe down the glove box with alcohol
options.D: Inspect the patient for skin allergies

explanation: You know it! Always wash or sanitize your hands before gloving up. Gloves don't replace hand hygiene! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: What should you do right away if your glove rips while caring for a patient?

options.A: Remove both gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on new ones
options.B: Apply a piece of adhesive plaster directly over the tear
options.C: Wash the torn glove with antiseptic soap while still wearing it
options.D: Continue the task quickly and change the gloves at the end

explanation: Safety first! A torn glove means your protective barrier is broken. Take them off, clean your hands, and start fresh with a new pair. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: When taking off your first glove, where should you grab it to start?

options.A: On the outside near the cuff area
options.B: At the thumb joint for better grip
options.C: At the fingertips to pull it straight off
options.D: On the inside near the wrist band

explanation: Spot on! Pinching the outer cuff lets you peel it safely without getting the outside germs onto your bare skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: How does turning the first glove inside out as you take it off protect you?

options.A: It neutralizes infectious agents through contact with air
options.B: It prevents the glove from sticking to the medical waste bag
options.C: It traps any collected pathogens on the inner side away from the skin
options.D: It stretches the rubber material to make it easier to throw away

explanation: Brilliant! Inverting the glove traps all the nasty germs safely on the inside so they never touch your hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of these actions is a dangerous infection control mistake when dealing with medical gloves?

options.A: Applying alcohol hand rub to soiled gloves
options.C: Inspecting the glove package before opening
options.D: Performing hand hygiene after glove removal

explanation: You've got it! Alcohol breaks down disposable gloves and ruins their protective power. Never sanitize dirty gloves—change them! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to wear just one single pair of gloves to care for two different patients in neighboring beds?

options.A: It causes severe skin breakdown and excessive sweating
options.B: It stretches the glove material beyond its elastic limit
options.C: It transfers microorganisms directly from one patient to another
options.D: It violates hospital billing and inventory policies

explanation: Spot on! Gloves pick up germs from patient number one; wearing them to patient number two spreads infection fast. Always change gloves between patients! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: Under which set of guidelines are gloves required for any task involving moist body fluids?
explanation: Great job! Standard Precautions are our baseline rules for every patient, keeping us safe from body fluids every single time. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)

question: A patient has a wound infection and is on Contact Precautions. When should you take off your gloves?

options.C: After walking out into the main hallway
options.D: Only when the entire shift comes to an end

explanation: You nailed it! Always take off your contact precaution gloves right inside the room before you touch doors or walk into the hallway. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)
